scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Marley's definitive death and Scrooge's unrelenting commitment to business above all else.
required_beats: Marley dies and his burial register is signed.
Scrooge conducts business even on the day of Marley's funeral.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Scrooge's cold misanthropy through his rejection of holiday goodwill, family connection, and charity.
required_beats: Scrooge works in his counting-house while keeping his clerk in the cold.
Scrooge's nephew arrives with Christmas cheer and a dinner invitation, which Scrooge harshly rejects.
Scrooge threatens to dismiss his clerk for applauding the nephew's sentiments.
Two portly gentlemen request charitable donations for the poor.
Scrooge refuses to give anything, dismisses the gentlemen, and returns to his work.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the wider city's festive preparations and contrasts the holiday spirit across different social strata.
required_beats: Labourers warm themselves around a brazier in the main street.
The Lord Mayor directs grand feast preparations at Mansion House.
The poor tailor's family prepares their modest holiday dinner.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Pays off Scrooge's utter hostility toward Christmas celebrations by showing his aggression toward a caroler.
required_beats: A boy sings a Christmas carol through the keyhole of the counting-house.
Scrooge grabs his ruler, terrifying the singer into fleeing.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Scrooge's begrudging concession to Christmas and his harsh treatment of his employee.
required_beats: Scrooge and the clerk prepare to close up the office.
Scrooge grudgingly allows the clerk Christmas Day off on the condition that he arrive earlier the next morning.
The clerk agrees, and Scrooge departs.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Shows the clerk's youthful joy and contrast to Scrooge's bleak demeanor upon being released from work.
required_beats: The clerk slides repeatedly down Cornhill in celebration.
The clerk hurries home toward Camden Town.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Illustrates Scrooge's joyless, habitual evening routine of total isolation.
required_beats: Scrooge eats his solitary dinner at his usual tavern, passing the time reading newspapers and checking his accounts.
Scrooge heads home toward his chambers.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Initiates the supernatural intrusion into Scrooge's tightly controlled, solitary existence.
required_beats: Scrooge sees Marley's face in the door knocker before it reverts to normal.
Scrooge enters, thoroughly searches his rooms to quell his apprehension, and double-locks himself inside.
Scrooge settles by the fire and tries to brush off his unease.
A disused room bell and then every bell in the house begin ringing uncontrollably before abruptly stopping.
A booming sound announces the opening of the cellar door.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To shatter Scrooge's denial and warn him of eternal damnation unless he submits to the visits of three spirits.
required_beats: Marley's ghost enters Scrooge's room, identifies himself, and forces Scrooge onto his knees in terror.
Marley explains the agonizing burden of his chains and warns Scrooge of the worse fate awaiting him.
Marley foretells the coming of Three Spirits as Scrooge's only chance of redemption.
Marley departs through the window, leaving Scrooge to observe wandering phantoms before falling asleep in bed.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To initiate the supernatural journey by introducing the Ghost of Christmas Past at the appointed hour.

char_scrooge.goal: lie awake until the hour was passed

required_beats: Scrooge awakens and waits anxiously in bed for the clock to strike one.
The Ghost of Christmas Past appears and reveals its identity and purpose.
Scrooge objects to the spirit's light but submits as the Ghost takes hold of him to depart.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To awaken Scrooge's dormant empathy and regret by confronting him with his lonely childhood.
required_beats: The Ghost brings Scrooge to the country road of his youth, where cheerful boys depart for the holidays.
They enter the schoolroom and find young Scrooge reading alone in neglect.
Scrooge weeps for his younger self and expresses regret over dismissing the boy who sang a carol the night before.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal the warmth and family affection Scrooge once possessed through the memory of his sister Fan.
required_beats: Fan bursts into the schoolroom to bring young Scrooge home with their father's blessing.
The schoolmaster receives the children in the parlour and provides refreshments.
Young Scrooge and Fan depart from the school in the chaise.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To remind Scrooge of the benevolence he once experienced from a master, awakening his conscience regarding his own treatment of Bob Cratchit.
required_beats: The Ghost brings Scrooge to Fezziwig's warehouse, which he recognizes with joy.
Fezziwig stops work and orders the warehouse cleared for a lively Christmas Eve dance.
The party unfolds with music, dancing, and warm hospitality from the Fezziwigs.
Scrooge passionately defends Fezziwig's generosity to the Ghost and realizes he wishes to speak with his own clerk.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To show the moment Scrooge chose wealth over love, sealing his path toward emotional isolation.
required_beats: Belle confronts young Scrooge with how greed has displaced his love for her.
Young Scrooge protests, but Belle releases him from their contract due to his changed nature.
Belle walks away, leaving young Scrooge alone.
An agonized Scrooge begs the Ghost to stop, but the Spirit forces him to watch one more shadow.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To confront Scrooge with the warm domestic life he sacrificed and his wretched isolation on the day Marley lay dying.
required_beats: The Ghost brings Scrooge into Belle's bustling, joyful home as the father returns with Christmas gifts.
After the children go to bed, Belle's husband mentions seeing a lonely Scrooge sitting solitary in his office while Marley lay dying.
Unable to bear the remorse and grief, Scrooge begs to leave and wrestles with the Ghost.
Scrooge extinguishes the Ghost's light by forcing the extinguisher cap down over its head.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To close the first Spirit's visitation and return Scrooge to the waking world.
required_beats: Scrooge finds himself back in his own bedroom and collapses into an exhausted sleep.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To introduce the Ghost of Christmas Present and mark Scrooge's growing willingness to be taught.

char_scrooge.goal: lie awake until the hour was passed
challenge the Spirit on the moment of its appearance

required_beats: The clock strikes one and Scrooge awakens to a ruddy light in his room.
Scrooge enters the adjoining transformed room and meets the Ghost of Christmas Present.
The Ghost reveals his identity and family of brothers to Scrooge.
Scrooge submits himself to be led and takes hold of the Spirit's robe.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal the benevolent nature of the Spirit's influence and challenge Scrooge's assumptions about holiday benevolence and piety.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Spirit appear in the busy city streets on Christmas morning.
The Spirit blesses the meals of the poor and calms quarreling dinner-carriers with his torch.
The Spirit explains the meaning of his blessing to Scrooge and clarifies that it applies most to the poor.
Scrooge questions the Spirit about sabbath restrictions, and the Ghost rejects responsibility for hypocritical mortals.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To transition the journey from the bustling city center out to the humble dwellings of the suburbs.
required_beats: The Ghost and Scrooge travel onward into the town's suburbs.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To show Scrooge the warmth, unity, and humble joy of Bob Cratchit's family preparing their Christmas feast.
required_beats: The Ghost brings Scrooge to Bob Cratchit's house and blesses the threshold.
Mrs. Cratchit and her children busy themselves preparing the holiday dinner.
Martha arrives home and plays a hiding trick on her father.
Bob Cratchit arrives with Tiny Tim, mourns Martha's supposed absence, and joyfully embraces her when she reveals herself.
The younger children take Tiny Tim to see the wash-house pudding preparations.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal Tiny Tim's gentle spirit and Bob's tender devotion to his son.
required_beats: Bob recounts Tiny Tim's wish that people in church saw his lameness to remember who made lame beggars walk.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To awaken Scrooge's sympathy for Tiny Tim and confront him with the human cost of his callous worldview.
required_beats: The Cratchit family serves their Christmas dinner and enjoys the goose and flaming pudding together.
Bob proposes a Christmas blessing and Tiny Tim blesses everyone.
Scrooge asks if Tiny Tim will live, and the Ghost rebukes him using Scrooge's own words about the surplus population.
Bob toasts Scrooge, prompting fierce reluctance from Mrs. Cratchit before the family drinks in silence.
The family converses about their modest prospects and Tiny Tim sings, after which the Spirit blesses them and the vision departs.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To transition Scrooge from the warmth of the Cratchit hearth into the wider world on Christmas Day.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Ghost of Christmas Present walk through the city streets.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate that Christmas joy and fellowship endure even in the most desolate and impoverished conditions.
required_beats: The Ghost brings Scrooge across a bleak moor inhabited by miners.
They enter a miner's hut where a multigenerational family gathers to sing a Christmas song together.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate that the spirit of Christmas reaches even the most isolated and remote outposts on earth.
required_beats: The Ghost takes Scrooge out across the sea.
Two solitary lighthouse keepers celebrate Christmas together with song and drink.
The Spirit and Scrooge visit a vessel far out over the water.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To show Scrooge how his family and peers view his isolation with amusement and pity rather than malice.
required_beats: The Spirit brings Scrooge to Fred's bright home, where the gathered company laughs warmly.
Fred recounts Scrooge's scorn for Christmas, defending him against the ladies' indignation by noting Scrooge only harms himself.
Fred resolves to continue extending his holiday invitation to Scrooge every year.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To awaken Scrooge's longing for connection and familial warmth as he witnesses his nephew's affection.
required_beats: The party engages in music and parlor games while Scrooge eagerly watches.
Scrooge pleads with the Ghost to let him linger as the fun continues.
Fred leads the company in a Christmas toast to Uncle Scrooge.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To confront Scrooge with the societal ruin caused by neglect and turn his own callous rhetoric back upon him.
required_beats: Scrooge notices the Spirit visibly aging as their travels draw to a close.
The Ghost reveals two wretched children, Ignorance and Want, hiding beneath its robes.
When Scrooge asks about their care, the Spirit turns Scrooge's own words about prisons and workhouses against him.
Midnight strikes and the Spirit vanishes.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Scrooge's terror and submission before the final, silent spirit of his visions.
required_beats: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come approaches Scrooge like a mist.
Scrooge kneels and asks if the Spirit will reveal what lies ahead.
The Spirit silently confirms by gesture.
Scrooge admits his deep fear but urges the Spirit to guide him forward.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Reveals the callous indifference of Scrooge's peers toward the unlamented death of an unnamed acquaintance.
required_beats: The Spirit brings Scrooge to 'Change and gestures toward a group of businessmen.
The merchants casually discuss an acquaintance's recent death and joke about attending his funeral only for the food.
Scrooge overhears another pair of acquaintances briskly remark that Old Scratch has claimed him.
Scrooge seeks himself in his customary corner and finds someone else in his place.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Exposes the grotesque violation of the dead man's possessions by predatory scavengers, striking dread into Scrooge.
required_beats: The Spirit takes Scrooge into a squalid rag-shop where three thieves gather with stolen bundles.
Old Joe leads them behind the screen and values the plunder brought by the undertaker's man and Mrs. Dilber.
The charwoman exhibits bed-curtains and the very shroud taken from the corpse.
Old Joe pays out their earnings while Scrooge recoils in horror, recognizing the lesson for his own life.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Pushes Scrooge to the verge of confronting the identity of the corpse, though his terror prevents him from looking.
required_beats: The Spirit brings Scrooge before an uncurtained bed holding a sheeted corpse.
The Spirit points relentlessly toward the covered head of the body.
Paralyzed by fear, Scrooge declares he cannot bring himself to uncover the face.
Scrooge implores the Spirit to show him anyone who feels any sorrow over this death.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate that the dead man's passing brings relief rather than sorrow to those who owed him.
required_beats: The Ghost reveals Caroline waiting anxiously with her children.
Caroline's husband returns and announces that their relentless creditor has died.
The couple feels relief and hopes for better terms under a new creditor.
Scrooge begs the Spirit to show him an example of tenderness connected with death.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To show the profound, loving grief in Bob Cratchit's household following the death of Tiny Tim.
required_beats: The Ghost brings Scrooge into the Cratchits' quiet and sorrowful home.
Bob Cratchit returns home and is comforted by his grieving family.
Bob breaks down over the loss of Tiny Tim and retreats upstairs to kiss his dead son.
Bob composes himself and rejoins the family downstairs.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To establish Fred's heartfelt kindness toward Bob Cratchit in a time of bereavement.
required_beats: Bob recounts meeting Scrooge's nephew Fred in the street.
Fred offers Bob heartfelt condolences and his business card for future assistance.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To conclude the Cratchits' tribute to Tiny Tim and prompt Scrooge to demand the identity of the unmourned dead man.
required_beats: The Cratchit family pledges never to forget Tiny Tim or his gentle spirit.
The family embraces Bob in shared love and reconciliation.
Scrooge asks the Spirit to reveal the identity of the dead man.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To build dread as Scrooge is denied sight of himself in his familiar surroundings, signaling his absence from the future.
required_beats: Scrooge is brought by the Ghost to the business district and asks to see his future self in his office.
The Ghost points elsewhere as Scrooge looks inside the office window.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To force Scrooge to confront his own impending doom and extract his final, desperate vow of transformation.
required_beats: The Ghost leads Scrooge to a neglected grave in a churchyard.
Scrooge reads his own name on the gravestone and realizes he is the unmourned dead man.
Scrooge desperately begs the Spirit for mercy and vows to honor Christmas and change his life.
Scrooge reaches for the Spirit's hand as the phantom pushes him away.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To show Scrooge waking restored to life and immediately channeling his joy into generous, frantic action.

char_scrooge.goal: challenge the Spirit on the moment of its appearance
send prize turkey to Bob Cratchit

required_beats: The phantom dissolves into a bedpost, leaving Scrooge overjoyed to find himself alive in his own chambers.
Scrooge learns from a passing boy that it is Christmas Day.
Scrooge hires the boy to purchase the prize turkey to send anonymously to Bob Cratchit.
Scrooge pays the poulterer's man and the boy, overwhelmed by sheer delight.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate Scrooge actively righting his past wrongs in the community and embracing the spirit of fellowship.
required_beats: Scrooge ventures into the streets in his finest clothes and receives warm greetings from passers-by.
Scrooge encounters the portly gentleman, begs his forgiveness, and pledges an astonishing donation.
Scrooge attends church and wanders the city taking joyful pleasure in all he sees.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reconcile Scrooge with his estranged nephew and rejoin the family circle he had previously scorned.
required_beats: Scrooge arrives at Fred's house and asks the maid if his nephew is at home.
Scrooge enters the dining room and asks Fred if he will let him join for dinner.
Fred joyfully welcomes his uncle into the celebration as the other guests arrive.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate the practical application of Scrooge's transformation through benevolence toward Bob Cratchit.
required_beats: Scrooge arrives early at the counting-house to wait for Bob Cratchit.
Bob hurries into the office late and tries to make up for lost time.
Scrooge feigns severity, calling Bob in to account for his tardiness.
Scrooge delights Bob by raising his salary and pledging support to his struggling family.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To resolve the story by confirming Scrooge's enduring transformation and Tiny Tim's survival.
required_beats: Scrooge becomes a second father to Tiny Tim and a genuinely benevolent presence to all.
